Who We Help
Military Members
Specialized Care for Military Members at Garden Springs Wellness

At Garden Springs Wellness Center, we respect and pay tribute to those who have served in the military, as well as veterans and their families. Military life can be very challenging during service and after. Although our service men and women are the picture of strength, many battle with things no one can see– from combat trauma and recovery, to deployment, to issues related to reintegrating into society, and military family life. If you or a loved one is struggling, there is hope and specialized treatment can help.

Here at Garden Springs Wellness Center, we provide professional,evidence-based mental health treatment for military members in NJ. We understand the unique needs of active duty members, veterans, and military families. Our mental health programs are designed to address your specific needs, including trauma, recovery, dual diagnosis, and any challenges you may face on the road to recovery. We have inpatient and outpatient mental health programs that are trauma-informed and will work with you to create a personalized treatment plan for recovery. Let us help you find solutions in a safe and supportive environment where you can learn to heal, gain strength and look forward to the future.
The Unique Mental Health Challenges Facing Military Members

Life in the military demands extraordinary mental and physical endurance. However, the experiences gained through service and the challenges faced along the way often leave lasting emotional and psychological wounds. Military members, veterans, and their families can carry the weight of these challenges long after their service, with many struggling to find the support they need to heal.
At Garden Springs Wellness Center, we provide care that directly addresses these unique mental health challenges:

Exposure to combat, life-threatening situations, or other high-stress environments can lead to post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) or unresolved trauma. These experiences can result in flashbacks, intrusive memories, hypervigilance, and emotional numbness that interfere with daily life.

blocks.text: The stresses of military service and reintegration into civilian life often contribute to feelings of anxiety and depression. Many military members report struggling with guilt, self-doubt, or feelings of isolation, which can worsen without support.

Returning home after deployment or transitioning into civilian life presents its own challenges. Military members must adapt to changes in their family dynamics, careers, and communities, often feeling misunderstood or out of place in civilian environments.

Substance use is a common concern for military members coping with mental health challenges. Alcohol or drug use is often used as a way to numb emotional pain, but without proper intervention, it can create additional barriers to healing.

We recognize that every military member’s journey is unique. Our programs are built to meet each individual at their starting point, providing understanding and tools for recovery that honor their service while addressing their specific needs.

Why Military-Informed Care Matters

Military members and veterans encounter unique stressors and experiences not often understood by the general population. Whether it’s the strain of deployment, the effects of combat, or the cultural norms of military life, these factors require a specialized approach to mental health treatment.

We believe that military personnel should have access to mental health services that take into consideration their unique experiences. That is why our treatment isn’t cookie-cutter. We use evidence-based treatments informed by years of working with military personnel and knowledge of military culture to provide you with effective care that promotes sustainable change. Some of the interventions we use in our therapy sessions include Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), which can help our clients identify and change unhelpful thought processes that are influencing their trauma, anxiety, and/or depression. Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) is another evidence-based trauma treatment that we provide to help you process traumatic memories less distressingly. Our treatment is also informed by trauma-informed care practices. Trauma-informed care creates a treatment environment that prioritizes safety, trustworthiness, and understanding of trauma. Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) skills are taught to help our clients better handle situations that are overwhelming or triggering. We provide veteran group therapy and military group therapy so that you can meet other veterans or military personnel with whom you can understand and connect with. We also offer family therapy to help improve communication and trust in your relationship with your loved ones. In addition to clinical work, we incorporate holistic methods such as mindfulness, exercise, and stress reduction into your treatment.
